chunks: Yunus narrated from Nasr ibn Habeeb, the owner of the inn (Al-Khan), who said:

I wrote to Abdullah ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'A sum of one hundred and four dirhams has come into my possession, and I am an innkeeper. The owner of the money died, and I do not know of any heirs for him. What is your opinion regarding informing me of its status and what I should do with it? For I have grown weary of holding it.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Work with it, and give it out as charity little by little until it is exhausted.'

key_terms.ضِقْتُ ذَرْعاً: I grew weary/tired of holding it

ai.seo_question: What should one do with a small amount of money found when the owner dies and no heirs are known?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of *khums* and charity principles for *mal al-mafqud* (lost property) when the owner is unknown, emphasizing gradual distribution to ensure the funds are effectively purified. The Imam’s instruction to 'work with it' suggests using the capital for trade to generate profit, which is then given as charity, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the finder acts as a trustee rather than an owner. This method ensures the small sum is fully expended in the path of God, avoiding the complexity of identifying specific recipients for such a minor amount.

en.hubeali: Yunus, from Nasr Bin Habeeb, the author of Al Khan, who said,

‘I wrote to Abd Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) that there were with me one hundred and forty Dirhams, and I am an owner of a hotel, and its owner (of the money) died, and I do not recognise any inheritor of his. So, your<sup>asws</sup> view in letting me know of its state and what shall I do with it, for I am fed up with it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘You can work in it and take out charity, little by little until it is taken out (completely)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Yunus has narrated from Nasr ibn Habib Sahib al-Khan who has narrated the following: “

I once wrote to the virtuous servant (of Allah) about two hundred and four dirham which remained with me. I own a hotel. The owner of dirham has died and I do not know any heirs for him. I need your opinion on this matter and what must I do about it; I am depressed thereby. He (the Imam) wrote and said, ‘You can work with it and give it as charity little by little until it is complete.’”
